Date: 2026-05-05
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: 56 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Lucia Gomez (Redwood CSM), Jordan Lee (ScoutLine Head of Platform), Priya Nair (ScoutLine ML Infra), Ethan Park (ScoutLine CTO)
summary: POC scoping focused on capacity sizing and autoscaling for a reserved GPU + burst strategy. Customer needs: deterministic p95 latency for user-facing endpoints, ability to absorb 3x traffic spikes during peak events, and strict data residency/SOC2 constraints. Agreed success metrics and initial benchmark plan; next steps include benchmark spreadsheet, traffic traces, and onboarding POC environment.
topics: Reserved GPUs vs hosted burst pools
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I see Jordan, Priya, Ethan — thanks for making time. Quick intros?
[00:12] Jordan Lee: Yeah hi, Jordan here, Head of Platform at ScoutLine. We run a conversational assistant across our support and product flows.
[00:20] Priya Nair: Priya, infra, I own our inference infra and cost model.
[00:25] Ethan Park: Ethan, CTO, oversight and budget owner.
[00:30] Maya Chen: Great, quick note on goal — scope a short POC to validate capacity sizing and autoscale fallback. Ravi, over to you for technical framing.
[00:38] Ravi Patel: Cool. So from Redwood's side, typical approach: reserved capacity for baseline throughput with a burst pool for 2-4x traffic surges. We'll run benchmarks for latency and tokens/sec and exercise fallback policies — e.g., model variant fallback and regional reroute.
[00:55] Jordan Lee: Important for us: user-facing SLO is p95 <= 350ms for short chat responses, and ability to handle spikes during product launches. Cost is also a factor, we don't want to pay for huge reserved pools.
[01:10] Priya Nair: Also need to validate prefix/KV cache behavior because we use a lot of contextual history; batch sizes vary between 1 and 8.
[01:22] Ravi Patel: Noted. For the POC we'll simulate both steady-state and spike patterns. Can you confirm typical token lengths and concurrency?
[01:30] Jordan Lee: Median request is 40-70 tokens, 95th is ~220 tokens. Concurrency averages 160 rps across all replicas, spikes go to ~500 rps for 10-15 minutes.
[01:45] Maya Chen: That's helpful. For reserved GPUs we usually size to cover baseline plus a safety buffer, then burst pool handles the short spikes. We also recommend a fallback model — smaller quantized variant — to keep latency bounded if the burst pool is saturated.
[02:05] Ethan Park: How graceful is the fallback? We can't have significant quality regressions for top 10 support flows.
[02:12] Ravi Patel: We do staged degradations: first try vertical autoscale within reserved pool, then burst to dedicated burst nodes, then fallback to a tuned smaller model with cached prefixes enabled. We'll run quality regression checks against a validation set to ensure top flows stay acceptable.
[02:30] Priya Nair: We need to see exact latencies under the fallback path — if fallback p95 jumps to 1s that's unacceptable.
[02:37] Maya Chen: Agreed. Success criteria draft: 1) baseline p95 <= 350ms; 2) under 3x traffic surge, 95% of requests either served by reserved+burst with p95 <= 600ms; 3) model-fallback path p95 <= 900ms and limited to non-critical flows.
[02:55] Jordan Lee: That seems reasonable as a starting point. Timeline? We want a quick win in 2-3 weeks.
[03:02] Maya Chen: POC timeline proposal: week 0 — exchange traces & sample prompts; week 1 — Redwood sets up reserved env and runs initial bench; week 2 — simulate spikes, run fallbacks, deliver report.
[03:14] Ravi Patel: For sizing, based on their numbers — baseline 160 rps median request size say 70 tokens => rough tokens/sec calculation => we estimate reserved capacity of 4 A40-equivalent GPUs (example) for target latency; burst pool add 2-3 GPUs for 3x spikes. But we'll validate with their traces.
[03:32] Ethan Park: A40s are fine, but can we support mixed GPU hardware? We have some on-prem with NVLink.
[03:38] Ravi Patel: Yes, Redwood supports heterogeneous pools; runtime will pick kernels accordingly, though perf varies. We'll note it in the benchmark.
[03:47] Priya Nair: Security — we need KMS, VPC peering, and SOC2 docs. Also audit logs for token-level access.
[03:56] Lucia Gomez: We can share SOC2 report and KMS integration guide. For Private deploys we support bring-your-own-KMS and VPC connectors.
[04:04] Jordan Lee: Any known limits around batching when KV cache is heavy?
[04:07] Ravi Patel: Good question — heavy KV cache reduces effective batch size because memory is used for KV. We'll test batch/sequence length tradeoffs in the bench. Also, continuous batching in the runtime will adapt but we should capture latency tail.
[04:20] Priya Nair: For benchmarks I want the config: model version, sequence length distribution, concurrency, and exact hardware.
[04:27] Maya Chen: We'll provide a benchmark spreadsheet with those fields. Link to shared template: https://app.redwood.example/benchmarks/scoutline-template (placeholder).
[04:36] Jordan Lee: On pricing — reserved vs usage — we'd like a comparison; we'll likely start with 3-month reserved commit if numbers look good.
[04:43] Maya Chen: We'll include pricing scenarios: monthly reserved with burst add-ons and a pay-as-you-go hosted fallback.
[04:49] Ethan Park: Can Redwood simulate regional failover? We need to see behavior if a region goes down.
[04:53] Ravi Patel: Yes we'll run a region-failure test: route traffic to secondary region and exercise model variant fallback. There will be an expected latency bump, we'll quantify.
[05:05] Jordan Lee: Who will run the bench? Redwood or ScoutLine?
[05:08] Maya Chen: We can run the main bench in Redwood's test harness against a reserved environment we provision; we'll ask you for traces and sample prompts to replay. If you prefer, your infra can run the client-side load.
[05:18] Priya Nair: We'll share traces and can run a couple of client-side tests if you provide the harness.
[05:22] Ravi Patel: Great — action item: we'll provide the harness and the benchmark config. We'll include metrics collection for p50/p95/p99 latency, token throughput, and cost per 1M tokens.
[05:33] Jordan Lee: What about privacy? Some prompts contain PII. We need to ensure data isn't logged to third parties.
[05:39] Lucia Gomez: For POC we'll enable data redaction and show options for customer-owned keys and no-persist modes. We'll document the retention and audit logs.
[05:47] Ethan Park: I want to see before/after quality metrics when fallback model used.
[05:50] Ravi Patel: We'll add automated rerank/accuracy checks on a prioritized test set for the top 20 flows. We'll report BLEU/ROUGE-like proxies and manual checks for subjective quality.
[06:02] Maya Chen: Ok recap — success criteria and timeline as discussed, Redwood to send benchmark template and SOC2/KMS docs, ScoutLine to send traces and sample prompts. We'll provision a reserved pool in our sandbox account and run bench week 1.
[06:15] Jordan Lee: Sounds good. Any blockers expected?
[06:18] Priya Nair: Need legal review for data handling but that's standard.
[06:21] Maya Chen: We'll attach the privacy annex and the POC data processing agreement for review.
[06:28] Ethan Park: Budget approved for POC. Let's target starting next Monday window.
[06:33] Maya Chen: We'll follow up with a calendar invite and the benchmark sheet. Thanks all.
[06:38] Jordan Lee: Thanks.
[06:40] Priya Nair: Thanks — bye.
[06:42] (call ends)
notes: Transcript contains occasional transcription errors (product names and acronyms). Customer emphasized p95 latency, 3x spike handling, KV cache impact on batching, and SOC2/KMS requirements. Redwood to run reserved+burst bench and provide pricing scenarios.
